Civil Revision No. 8994 of 1991 (Dhaka) 
Civil Revision No. 311 of 1989 (Rangpur)
lawyer:
Shaheed Alam, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Md. Ismail and Abdur Rahim, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Party Nos. 1(a) to 1(d).
parties:
Haragram Trust Board ------ Petitioner
vs
Dr. Golam Mortuza Hossain ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment: 7. It appears from paragraph 2 of the plaint that the following averment was made by the plaintiff: "At the time of departure of previous tenant Dr. Lutfar Rahman, the defendant applied to the Trust Board on 26 November, 1962 for using the suit premises as dispensary only and he entered the suit premises with an agreement to pay rent at the rate of Taka 20.00 per month according to English Calendar." Defendant did not deny the same in his written statement but in paragraph 12 of the written statement he admitted that Dr. Lutfar Rahman was in possession of the suit premises having been inducted therein by the previous tenant Dr. Bhupendra Nath Bhuiyan and the said Dr. Lutfar Rahman transferred the suit premises to him on 26.11.1962. Deposing as PW 1 on behalf of the plaintiff Managing Trustee Md. Shah Newaz stated that Dr. Bhupendra Nath was a tenant in the suit premises under the Trust and thereafter Dr. Lutfar Rahman was a tenant. Then defendant prayed for taking lease in the last part of 1962 at a monthly rent of Taka 20.00 and paid rent for 3/4 months and defendant applied on 26.11.62 for using the suit premises as dispensary and in the application defendant signed his name in his presence. Application dated 26.11.62 has been marked as Ext. 13, notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act issued on 2.11.86 has been marked as Ext. 17 and the postal acknowledgement receipt signed by the defendant on 3.11.86 has been marked as Ext. 18. Signature of defendant Golam Mortuza Hossain appearing in the vokalatnama filed by him on 29.1.87 in the Court below tallies with his signature appearing in the postal acknowledgement receipt Ext. 18 and both the said signatures tally with his signature appearing in Ext. 13. From Ext. 13 it appears that Dr. Lutfar Rahman used the suit premises as a tenant of plaintiff Trust as his dispensary and defendant wanted to hire the same at monthly rent of Taka 20.00 and he agreed to pay rent at the end of every month. Though defendant denied in his deposition that he did not submit the application on 26.11.62 for hiring suit premises and writing and signature appearing therein are not his it was incumbent upon the Court below to compare his signatures in English appearing in the vokalatnama filed by him on 29.1.87 and the postal acknowledgement receipt Ext. 18 with his signature appearing in the application dated 26.11.62 (Ext.13). Without doing so Court below found fault with the plaintiff for not proving Ext. 13 legally merely relying upon denial of the defendant. When a document is produced by a party and the signature appearing therein is proved and the document is marked as an exhibit without objection from the other side and subsequently other side denies signature appearing therein it is the duty of the Court to compare the said signature with his other admitted signatures on record. Thus the Court below acted illegally in not relying upon the said Ext. 13 and in holding that the defendant did not admit the plaintiff as tenant and that question of title is involved between the parties merely relying upon an entry in the RS Khatian recording his name of the defendant in permissive possession of the suit property and also relying on rent receipts and municipal tax receipts. From consideration of the above facts and circumstances and evidence on record it is clear that the defendant was a tenant in the suit premises since 26.11.62 and his claim of title has no basis.
